what: Sysco is the largest food distributor in the world. It buys food and supplies and delivers them to restaurants, hospitals, schools, hotels and other places where meals are prepared away from home.
customers: Independent restaurants above all, plus chains, healthcare and education caterers, and hotels.
money: food distribution across the United States
Canada, the United Kingdom, France and Latin America
moat: A distribution network of warehouses and trucks reaching hundreds of thousands of kitchens, where delivery reliability matters more than price for independent restaurants.
risks: Net margin of about 2% is thin, as is normal in distribution
Restaurant traffic falls when consumers cut back on eating out
Food cost inflation and deflation both disrupt its pricing
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 14% is good for a distributor
Independent restaurants, its most profitable customers, are growing as a share of cases
Analysts see about 18% upside from current levels
watch: US case volume growth, especially to local independent restaurants.
